where: hir-def tests that count queries by name (nameres/frozen/entries/tests.rs, nameres/frozen/items/tests.rs)
what: Two 'no parse / no expansion' tests passed whatever the code did: they filtered the run log by substrings (`parse`, `outline`, `macro_expand`) and asserted the filtered list empty. `macro_expand` names no query of the tree; and a fixture database has parsed every file and compiled every `macro_rules!` expander by the time a test asks (name resolution runs when the fixture is made), so no parse query runs with or without the feature. Their controls were what failed, the first time anything ran.
cost: about a fifth of the lane's context reading why an empty list was empty
cause: an absence asserted by a substring over names nobody listed, in a database that had already done the work the test says is saved
class: vacuous success: an absence check with no proof the thing can be present
prevention: each control now asserts the exact names that run (items) or the store's own counts (entries); not built: a test-database way to start with nothing resolved (lib served from records) so 'no parse' can be shown, and a list of the run log's query names tests match exactly instead of by substring
workaround: count what the store made and found (`Counts`), not query names
fix: tests rewritten in the int-1112 tree; the parse saved by kept macro definitions is still shown by no test
